rendered: The anode-free full cell uses pyrite (iron disulfide) as its cathode: pyrite (FeS2) for the cathode[1]. Because pyrite contains no sodium natively, it is presodiated before assembly: presodiated the pyrite cathode prior to cell assembly[2]. The cells are built from presodiated pyrite paired with carbon/Al current collectors in a discharged state, and sodium is then plated in situ on the carbon/Al during the first charge, so the cell does not contain sodium metal on assembly[3]. For the energy density, the cathode capacity assumed was 335 mAh/g[4] (with a Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry), applied to the mass of the presodiated pyrite and the carbon nucleation layer.
